content.text:
**Finding: compliant (no redline proposed).**

The IP allocation sits at or above the playbook fallback:

| Element | Where met |
|---|---|
| Vendor retains only pre-existing/generic tech | 3.3 (p0253) retained rights limited to RevMed Licensed Technology |
| Customer owns/receives assignment of outputs | 1.109/1.110 (Sanofi Sole Program Technology); 6.2 (p0339) "hereby does assign, to Sanofi all of its rights, title and interests in and to all Regulatory Approvals" |
| Perpetual / irrevocable / royalty-free | 12.3(b) (p0499) on expiration |
| Worldwide | Licensed Territory = "all countries and territories of the world" |
| Use, exploit and sublicense for our business | 3.1 (p0248) and 3.4(b) (p0256), multiple tiers |
| Vendor licence in our materials limited to service delivery | 3.2 (p0252) "solely to the extent necessary for RevMed to perform its obligations" |

Noted in the rationale rather than flagged: joint ownership of Joint Program Technology departs from the preferred "no joint ownership" element, but 10.1(b) confers an unrestricted right to exploit and license without accounting or consent, plus an irrevocable, perpetual, fully-paid, worldwide, sublicensable cross-licence — so it is not walk-away and does not warrant a redline. The 12.3(c) reversion of Regulatory Approvals on termination is a termination-consequence term and is not double-flagged here.
